grf.observed: Merged v1 resolves every canonical use target by exact module identity, including plain MODULE-mode uses.
grf.generated_hypothesis: Plain use A.B denotes an exact module B whenever an exact module provider exists.
grf.counter_reality: Plain use A.B can denote an exported name B from parent module A, so exact path shape alone is insufficient to choose module-provider semantics.
grf.discriminating_observation: Authorized corpus: claycode/frank_memory.clay declares `use frank.entity.Frank`; claycode/frank_entity.clay declares `module frank.entity` and exports `entity Frank`, not module frank.entity.Frank.
grf.collapse: The generic v1 plain-use exact-module interpretation is REFUTED_AS_CANONICAL_SEMANTICS. Exact provider lookup remains useful only where module semantics are independently justified, such as a future proven wildcard-module contract.

product_coordination.reason: Exposing the v1 resolver through ClayEnv would make an overbroad plain-use interpretation more accessible even though executable use remained fail-closed.
product_coordination.correction_candidate_scope: ClayPackageResolution/v2 WILDCARD_MODULE_PROVIDER_ONLY; plain MODULE use fails PLAIN_USE_NAME_BINDING_UNSELECTED

unusual_experiment.name: NEAR_PREFIX_MISSING_TARGET_DECEPTION
unusual_experiment.environment: isolated in-memory mechanism probe mirroring the merged v1 exact dictionary lookup branch
unusual_experiment.baseline: exact clay.lib.util key present -> selected provider
unusual_experiment.intervention: remove exact key; retain only clay.lib.utility and clay.lib.util.extra
unusual_experiment.interpretation: v1 does not fall back to near-prefix names; this does not prove that plain use denotes a module.

next_falsifier: Obtain exact-head self-hosted evidence for the v2 correction that resolves only syntactically explicit wildcard-module providers while rejecting all plain MODULE uses as name-binding-unselected; only then design the smallest explicit plain-name/export visibility contract from authorized corpus evidence.
